s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of unilateral lower extremity numbness, pain, and weakness, worsening over time, with evidence of nerve dysfunction
salient_findings: Muscle weakness in the right tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, gastrocnemius, and flexor hallucis longus
key_facts: 48-year-old woman with a history of asthma
2-day history of right lower-extremity numbness and pain
No low back pain
Manual muscle testing showed weakness in the right tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus
Deep-tendon reflexes were normal
Straight-leg-raising was positive at 70 degrees
Femoral-nerve stretch test was negative
Degenerative scoliosis at L5-S1 on plain radiographs
Right-sided disc herniation at L5-S1 on lumbar MRI
No significant nerve-root or cord compression on lumbar MRI
Decreased ankle-brachial indices
No significant vascular lesions on lower-extremity arteriography
Initial peroneal-nerve conduction studies showed a motor conduction velocity of 51.5 m/s
Muscle strength nearly normalized by day 7, but lateral leg pain persisted
Pain increased by day 22, and right foot drop developed by day 26
Urgent MRI showed no new nerve-root compression
Repeat peroneal conduction studies failed to elicit an evoked myogenic potential

shortlist.label: L5 radiculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral lower extremity numbness, pain, and weakness, with evidence of nerve dysfunction and degenerative scoliosis at L5-S1

shortlist.label: Peroneal nerve palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Foot drop and weakness in the tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus, with decreased motor conduction velocity on peroneal-nerve conduction studies

shortlist.label: Lumbosacral plexopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Worsening lower extremity numbness, pain, and weakness, with evidence of nerve dysfunction and degenerative scoliosis at L5-S1

shortlist.label: Fibular neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Foot drop and weakness in the peroneus longus, with decreased motor conduction velocity on peroneal-nerve conduction studies

shortlist.label: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower extremity weakness and numbness, with evidence of nerve dysfunction and absent Achilles reflexes

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including right lower-extremity numbness and pain, weakness in the right tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus, and development of right foot drop, are consistent with peroneal nerve palsy. The initial peroneal-nerve conduction studies showed a decreased motor conduction velocity, and repeat studies failed to elicit an evoked myogenic potential, further supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: L5 radiculopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and examination findings are more consistent with a peripheral nerve lesion rather than a radiculopathy, and the lumbar MRI showed no significant nerve-root compression.

rejected.label: Lumbosacral plexopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are localized to the peroneal nerve distribution, rather than a more widespread plexopathy.

rejected.label: Fibular neuropathy
rejected.why: Fibular neuropathy is a less specific term that could be a part of the peroneal nerve palsy, but peroneal nerve palsy is a more specific and accurate diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and examination findings are more consistent with a localized peripheral nerve lesion rather than a widespread polyneuropathy.
